In California:

### 1. Professional corporation - recurring Secretary of State filing

**Report:** Statement of Information

> "Generally, CA Stock Corporations and Qualified Out-of-State Corporations are required to file their Statement of Information yearly in the month of registration with the California Secretary of State."

> "A Statement of Information must be filed either every year for California stock, cooperative, credit union, and all qualified out-of-state corporations"

A professional corporation is a corporation for this filing rule. The opened Secretary of State FAQ page does not separately state a different frequency for professional / accountancy or law corporations.

**Fee:**

The opened Secretary of State FAQ page states only:

> "The fee for filing a Statement of Information is $20 or $25."

Which entity pays $20 versus $25 was not stated with breakdown on the pages opened, so it wasn't found and is not stated here instead of guessing.

### 2. LLC - recurring Secretary of State filing

**Report:** Statement of Information

> "California Nonprofit Corporations and all Limited Liability Companies are required to file every two years in the month of registration in even or odd years based on the year of registration."

> "two years (only in odd years or only in even years based on year of initial registration) for California nonprofit corporations and all California and qualified out-of-state limited liability companies."

> "California and Out-of-State Limited Liability Company: File online at bizfileOnline.sos.ca.gov the Statement of Information – CA and Out-of-State LLC."

**Fee:**

> "The fee for filing a Statement of Information is $20 or $25."

Which amount applies to LLCs was not stated with breakdown on the pages opened, so it wasn't found and is not stated here instead of guessing.

### 3. Yearly state franchise / minimum / annual tax

**LLC:**

> "Every LLC that is doing business or organized in California must pay an annual tax of $800."

> "This yearly tax will be due, even if you are not conducting business, until you cancel your LLC."

> "Pay the $800 annual tax"

> "To keep your LLC active you must:"

> "File and pay your state income taxes"

**Professional corporation:**

Whether a yearly $800 minimum franchise tax or other franchise tax applies to a professional corporation was not stated on the official pages opened for this answer, so it wasn't found and is not stated here instead of guessing.
